prompt: For $R\subseteq A\times A$, which condition defines symmetry? All quantified variables range over $A$.

answers.explanation: Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required.
Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This defines reflexivity, not symmetry.
No element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This defines irreflexivity, not symmetry.
Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices. This defines transitivity, not symmetry.
Mutual relatedness forces equality. Self-loops are allowed. This defines antisymmetry, not symmetry.
Every related pair has no reverse. Taking the two elements equal also forbids loops. This defines asymmetry, not symmetry.
Every pair of distinct elements is comparable in at least one direction. This convention imposes no condition on loops. This defines connexity on distinct elements, not symmetry.
Two outgoing neighbours of the same element must be related in the indicated direction. This defines the right-euclidean property, not symmetry.
Every related pair is diagonal; some or all loops may be missing. This defines coreflexivity, not symmetry.
Some related pair lacks its reverse; this is an existential violation. This defines failure of symmetry, not symmetry.
